newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen up on carry-over, peso weaker.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen up on carry-over, peso weaker.

text.p: --Peso likely weak ahead of U.S. data
--Cetes overnight rate viewed up on tight liquidity
Traders saw stocks opening with mild upside potential on Thursday due to substantial momentum gathered in Tuesday's and Wednesday's record-breaking rally.
"Blue chips have all broken out and the bourse has a lot of inherent strength still," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts situated resistance at 4,135 points on the IPC index, compared to Wednesday's close of 4,121.56.
Dealers expected the peso to open weaker with brokers covering short dollar positions ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday and their possible impact on the U.S. bond market.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9300/7.9500 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9330/7.9380 per dollar, compared to Wednesday's close of 7.9230/7.9265.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening up from Wednesday's close of 19.00 percent on a weak peso and liquidity pressures.
